2027-08-06.title: The Transfiguration of Our Lord
readings: His face shone like the sun
Who shall ascend the hill of the Lord?
The Lord will be your everlasting light
We were eyewitnesses of his majesty
O the depth of the riches and wisdom of God
This is my Son, my Chosen; listen to him
2027-08-06.alt: Feast of the Transfiguration (M'thale). The season of the Transfiguration begins. The Fifteen Days' Fast continues until 15 August.
2027-08-06.verse: Then from the cloud came a voice that said, “This is my Son, my Chosen; listen to him!”
theo: Jesus takes Peter, John and James up the mountain to pray. “And while he was praying, the appearance of his face changed, and his clothes became dazzling white.” Moses and Elijah appear in glory and speak with him “of his departure, which he was about to accomplish at Jerusalem.” The Law and the Prophets bear witness to Christ, and they speak of the Cross. The glory of Tabor and the darkness of Calvary belong together.

Peter, overwhelmed, says: “Master, it is good for us to be here; let us make three dwellings, one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” The Old Testament reading recalls the Feast of Booths, when Israel lived in tents to remember God's care in the desert. But a cloud overshadows them, the cloud of God's presence, and a voice says: “This is my Son, my Chosen; listen to him!” When the voice has spoken, “Jesus was found alone.” He is the true dwelling of God among us.

At Sinai God came down on the mountain in fire and cloud, and the people could not approach. On Tabor the glory of God shines in the face of a man, and the disciples are touched by him: “Get up and do not be afraid.” St Peter later writes that he and the others “were eyewitnesses of his majesty… we ourselves heard this voice come from heaven, while we were with him on the holy mountain.” Our faith rests on what the apostles saw and heard.

The Transfiguration shows us our own future. The light that shone from Christ is the glory he will share with those who belong to him. Isaiah says: “The LORD will be your everlasting light, and your God will be your glory.” Paul can only exclaim: “O the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God!” In the season that now begins, the Church contemplates the glory of Christ and prepares for his coming.
conn: Sinai and Tabor.
Exodus 19–20: God speaks from the mountain; Tabor: the Father speaks of the Son.
Booths and tents.
Deuteronomy 16: the Feast of Booths; Peter's three tents; Christ is God's true tent among us (John 1:14).
The hill of the Lord.
Psalm 24:3–4: “Who shall ascend the hill of the LORD?… Those who have clean hands and pure hearts.”
Everlasting light.
Isaiah 60:19: no need of sun or moon; the Lord is our light.
altar: What the three apostles saw on the mountain we receive veiled at the altar. The same Christ who shone on Tabor is present in the Holy Mysteries; one day the veil will be lifted, and we shall see him as he is.
outline: The light he will share with us.
“This is my Son, my Chosen; listen to him!”
live: Climb the mountain
Spend fifteen minutes in silent prayer today, perhaps before the Blessed Sacrament.
Listen to him
Choose one word of Jesus to obey this week.
Keep the fast
Continue the Fifteen Days' Fast with joy, in honour of Mary.
fathers: St Leo the Great

The principal purpose of the Transfiguration was to remove the scandal of the Cross from the disciples' hearts, so that the humiliation of his voluntary suffering would not disturb the faith of those to whom the glory of his hidden dignity had been revealed (Sermon 51, 3).
St Anastasius of Sinai
“It is good for us to be here.” Let us hasten there with confidence and joy, to enter the cloud like Moses and Elijah, or like James and John (Homily on the Transfiguration).
magis: Catechism 554–556
The Transfiguration gives a foretaste of Christ's glorious coming; the whole Trinity appears: the Father in the voice, the Son in the man, the Spirit in the shining cloud.
Catechism 568
Christ's Transfiguration aims at strengthening the apostles' faith in anticipation of his Passion.
Catechism 1000
Our sharing in Christ's glory is the hope of the resurrection.
saints: Sunday 8 August: I Sunday after the Transfiguration. 10 August: St Lawrence. 14 August: St Maximilian Kolbe. Sunday 15 August: Shunoyo, the Assumption of Mary, Mother of God.
2027-08-06.prayer: Lord Jesus, transfigured on the holy mountain, you showed your disciples the glory that was yours before the Cross. Teach us to listen to you, to go up the mountain in prayer, and to come down again to serve; and bring us at last to see your face in the light that never fades. Amen.

2027-08-08.title: First Sunday after the Transfiguration
readings: A lamp on the lampstand; the seed that grows by itself
A faithful priest I will raise up
Elijah on Carmel: the Lord, he is God
Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you
Whatever is true, whatever is honourable
2027-08-08.alt: Season of the Transfiguration. The Fifteen Days' Fast continues; Sunday 15 August is the Shunoyo (Assumption).
2027-08-08.verse: “Which of the two did the will of his father?” They said, “The first.”
theo: A father has two sons. He says to the first, “Son, go and work in the vineyard today.” He answers, “I will not”; but later he changes his mind and goes. The second answers, “I go, sir”; but he does not go. “Which of the two did the will of his father?” The answer is obvious, and it is uncomfortable. Words are easy; obedience is what counts. Jesus adds that tax collectors and prostitutes, who repented at John's preaching, are going into the kingdom ahead of those who said all the right words.

In the evening Gospel Jesus says: “Is a lamp brought in to be put under the bushel basket, or under the bed, and not on the lampstand?” Faith is not meant to be hidden. And he tells of seed that a man scatters on the ground; “the seed would sprout and grow, he does not know how… first the stalk, then the head, then the full grain in the head.” God makes his kingdom grow; our part is to sow faithfully and to let our light be seen.

Deuteronomy demands honesty in daily business: “You shall have only a full and honest weight; you shall have only a full and honest measure, so that your days may be long in the land.” Faith shows itself in the market, the office and the fields. On Carmel Elijah prays: “Answer me, O LORD, so that this people may know that you, O LORD, are God”; the fire falls, and the people cry: “The LORD indeed is God!” A people that says “yes” to God must also live it.

St James calls us: submit yourselves to God; resist the devil and he will flee from you; draw near to God and he will draw near to you; humble yourselves before the Lord and he will exalt you (James 4:7–10). St Paul tells the Philippians to think about whatever is true, honourable, just, pure, pleasing and commendable, and to do what they have learned (Philippians 4:8–9). That is the son who goes into the vineyard.
conn: Honest measures.
Deuteronomy 25:15: integrity in daily life is part of obedience.
The faithful priest.
1 Samuel 2:35: God raises up a priest who will do what is in his heart; Christ is that faithful priest.
The Lord is God.
1 Kings 18:39: the people's confession on Carmel; Elijah appeared with Christ on Tabor.
The end.
Ezekiel 7: the day of reckoning; the season of the Transfiguration looks toward Christ's coming.
altar: In the Holy Qurbono we say “Amen” many times. The two sons remind us that our “Amen” at the altar must become a “yes” in the vineyard of our daily life.
outline: The will of the Father is done, not only spoken.
Point 2 · A lamp on the stand
Faith is not to be hidden.
“Which of the two did the will of his father?”
live: Turn a “no” into a “yes”
Do one thing this week that you have long been refusing God.
Honest measure
Be scrupulously honest in one business or work matter this week.
Think on what is true
Replace one hour of gossip or bad media with something good and true.
fathers: St John Chrysostom
Jesus shows that it is better to promise nothing and do it, than to promise and fail; and he opens the door of repentance to those who first refused (Homilies on Matthew 67).
St Jerome
The first son is the Gentiles and sinners, who first refused and then obeyed; the second is those who said “we will do” at Sinai and did not (Commentary on Matthew 3).
magis: Catechism 2826
By prayer we can discern the will of God and obtain the endurance to do it.
Catechism 2409–2411
Any form of unjustly taking and keeping the property of others, including false weights and fraud, is against the seventh commandment.
Catechism 1432
The human heart is converted by looking upon him whom our sins have pierced; it is never too late to say yes.
saints: 10 August: St Lawrence. 14 August: St Maximilian Kolbe. Sunday 15 August: Shunoyo, the Assumption of Mary, Mother of God, and Independence Day of India.
2027-08-08.prayer: Father, you call us to work in your vineyard today. Forgive our empty promises and turn our refusals into obedience. Make us honest in every measure, let our faith shine like a lamp on its stand, and draw us near to you as you draw near to us. Amen.

2027-08-15.title: Shunoyo: the Assumption of Mary, Mother of God
readings: Here are my mother and my brothers
I will put enmity between you and the woman
At your right hand stands the queen
Let the earth open, that salvation may sprout
The tent of testimony; the Most High does not dwell in houses made by hands
The ark of the covenant; Christ entered the holy place
2027-08-15.alt: Feast of the Shunoyo (Assumption of Mary, Mother of God): Holy Qurbono for the people. The Fifteen Days' Fast ends. Also Independence Day of India (80th anniversary) and the anniversary of the founding of the Bethany Ashram (1919).
2027-08-15.verse: Then he said to the disciple, “Here is your mother.” And from that hour the disciple took her into his own home.
theo: Today the Church celebrates the Shunoyo, the “departure” of the Mother of God. The Eastern Churches sing of her Dormition, her falling asleep in the Lord; the Catholic Church professes, as defined by Pope Pius XII in 1950, that “the Immaculate Mother of God, the ever-virgin Mary, having completed the course of her earthly life, was assumed body and soul into heavenly glory.” The body that carried the Son of God was not left to corruption. Where Christ the Head has gone, his Mother has followed, and where she is, we hope to be.

The Old Testament readings speak of the ark. The ark of the covenant held the tablets of the Law, the manna and Aaron's rod; when the priests carried it into the Jordan, the waters parted and the people crossed into the promised land. The Letter to the Hebrews describes that tabernacle with its ark. The Fathers saw in Mary the true Ark of the Covenant: she carried within her the Word, the Bread of Life, the true High Priest. Today the Ark crosses the Jordan of death into the promised land of heaven.

From the beginning God promised: “I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; he will strike your head.” The woman who stands against the serpent is fulfilled in Mary, the New Eve. Psalm 45 sings: “at your right hand stands the queen in gold of Ophir.” Mary, assumed into heaven, stands beside her Son as Queen, not to rule apart from him, but to intercede for his brothers and sisters.

At the foot of the Cross Jesus says to his mother: “Woman, here is your son,” and to the disciple: “Here is your mother. And from that hour the disciple took her into his own home.” And in the evening Gospel: “whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother.” Mary is mother because she heard God's word and kept it perfectly. The Assumption is the reward of that faithful “yes”, and a promise for all who do the Father's will.
conn: The New Eve.
Genesis 3:15: the woman and her offspring against the serpent; Revelation 12: the woman clothed with the sun.
The Ark.
Joshua 4 and Hebrews 9: the ark of the covenant; Mary, the living Ark who carried the Word made flesh.
The Queen.
Psalm 45:9: the queen at the king's right hand; Mary crowned in glory beside her Son.
The tent of God.
Acts 7:44–49: God does not dwell in houses made by hands; he dwelt in the womb of the Virgin.
altar: In the anaphora the Church remembers “our Lady, the holy and ever-virgin Mother of God, Mary” before all the saints. At the altar heaven and earth are joined; Mary, assumed into glory, worships with us the Son she bore.
outline: The Shunoyo: Mary's departure into glory.
What the Church believes and why.
Point 2 · The Ark crosses the Jordan
Mary, the living Ark of the Covenant.
Point 3 · The woman and the serpent
The New Eve and the Queen.
live: Take her home
Renew a family consecration to Mary or pray the Rosary together tonight.
Pray for India
On Independence Day, pray for the nation, its poor and its peace.
Respect the body
Honour your body and others' bodies as destined for glory.
fathers: St John of Damascus

It was fitting that she who had kept her virginity intact in childbirth should keep her own body free from all corruption even after death; that she who had carried the Creator as a child at her breast should dwell in the divine tabernacles (Homily 2 on the Dormition, cited in Munificentissimus Deus).
St Jacob of Serugh
The Syriac poet sang of the Virgin's departure, accompanied by the apostles and received by her Son into the bridal chamber of light (Homily on the Burial of the Holy Mother of God).
magis: Munificentissimus Deus 44 (Pius XII, 1950)
Mary, having completed the course of her earthly life, was assumed body and soul into heavenly glory.
Catechism 966
The Assumption of the Blessed Virgin is a singular participation in her Son's Resurrection and an anticipation of the resurrection of other Christians.
Lumen Gentium 68
Mary, glorified in body and soul, is the image and beginning of the Church as it is to be perfected in the world to come, a sign of sure hope and comfort.
saints: In 2027 the II Sunday after the Transfiguration falls on this day and gives way to Shunoyo. Sunday 22 August: III Sunday after the Transfiguration; Social Justice Sunday.
2027-08-15.prayer: Almighty God, you took up the Immaculate Virgin Mary, Mother of your Son, body and soul into heavenly glory. Grant that, taking her into our homes as the beloved disciple did, and doing your will as she did, we may follow her into the joy of your kingdom. Bless our nation India with justice and peace. Amen.

2027-08-22.title: Third Sunday after the Transfiguration
readings: Ask, and it will be given you
Noah found favour in the sight of the Lord
Do not turn your face from the poor
When you pass through the waters, I will be with you
Scoffers will come in the last days
My grace is sufficient for you
God, be merciful to me, a sinner
2027-08-22.alt: Season of the Transfiguration. Social Justice Sunday: the offering of the Holy Qurbono is sent to the eparchial centre for the welfare fund of Dalit Christians. The Eight Days' Fast in honour of the Nativity of Mary begins on Wednesday 1 September.
2027-08-22.verse: But the tax collector, standing far off, would not even look up to heaven, but was beating his breast and saying, “God, be merciful to me, a sinner!”
theo: Two men go up to the temple to pray. The Pharisee stands and prays about himself: “God, I thank you that I am not like other people: thieves, rogues, adulterers, or even like this tax collector.” The tax collector stands far off, will not lift his eyes, beats his breast and says: “God, be merciful to me, a sinner!” Jesus says: “this man went down to his home justified rather than the other.” Prayer is not a report of our achievements; it is the cry of a poor heart before God's mercy.

The tax collector's prayer has become the prayer of the Eastern Churches: “Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner.” Our Qurbono is full of “Kurielaison”, Lord have mercy. Ecclesiastes warns: “Guard your steps when you go to the house of God… God is in heaven, and you upon earth; therefore let your words be few.” God does not need many words, but an honest and humble heart.

In the evening Gospel Jesus teaches perseverance: a man goes to his friend at midnight asking for three loaves; because of his persistence the friend gets up and gives him what he needs. “So I say to you, Ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you… how much more will the heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him!” Humble prayer is also bold and persistent.

St Paul, given great revelations, received “a thorn in the flesh”. Three times he begged the Lord to remove it, and the Lord said: “My grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness.” So Paul boasts of his weakness, “so that the power of Christ may dwell in me… for whenever I am weak, then I am strong” (2 Corinthians 12:9–10). The tax collector's weakness, offered to God, becomes the place of grace.
conn: Noah found favour.
Genesis 6:8–9: in a corrupt generation Noah walked with God; grace, not pride, saves.
Few words.
Ecclesiastes 5:2: “let your words be few”; the tax collector's seven-word prayer.
The poor.
Sirach 4:4: “Do not reject a suppliant in distress”; God does not reject the humble sinner.
Through the waters.
Isaiah 43:2: God is with us in every trial; Paul's thorn.
altar: Before receiving the Holy Mysteries we pray with the tax collector, acknowledging our unworthiness. The Lord who justified him comes to us not because we are good, but because he is merciful.
outline: Point 1 · I thank you that I am not like others
Point 2 · Be merciful to me, a sinner
The prayer of the humble heart.
“God, be merciful to me, a sinner!”
live: Pray the Jesus Prayer
Repeat during the day: “Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner.”
No comparisons
Notice when you compare yourself favourably with others, and stop.
Prepare for the Eight Days' Fast
Plan prayer and fasting from 1 to 8 September in honour of Mary's Nativity.
fathers: St Augustine
The Pharisee came to the physician and showed his healthy parts, hiding his wounds; the tax collector showed his wounds, and was healed (Sermon 115, 2).
St John Chrysostom
Humility makes the sinner righteous; pride makes the righteous a sinner. The tax collector, by confessing, went down justified (On the Incomprehensible Nature of God 5).
magis: Catechism 2559
Humility is the foundation of prayer; only when we humbly acknowledge that we do not know how to pray as we ought are we ready to receive the gift.
Catechism 2613
The parables of the importunate friend and the Pharisee and tax collector teach persistence and humility in prayer.
Catechism 2667
The invocation of the holy name of Jesus, the Jesus Prayer, is the simplest way of praying always.
saints: 28 August: St Augustine. Sunday 29 August: Beheading of St John the Baptist; St Euphrasia. 1 September (Wed): the Eight Days' Fast begins.
2027-08-22.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner. Free us from the pride that compares and despises; teach us to pray with humility and persistence; and let your grace be sufficient for us, your power made perfect in our weakness. Amen.

2027-08-29.title: Fourth Sunday after the Transfiguration
readings: The mother of the sons of Zebedee
The Lord is the Levites' inheritance
Act faithfully, with your whole heart
Happy are those whose way is blameless
Serve one another with whatever gift each has received
He emptied himself, taking the form of a slave
The Son of Man came not to be served but to serve
2027-08-29.alt: Season of the Transfiguration. Malankara Catholic Mothers' Forum (MCMF) Day. Beheading of St John the Baptist; St Euphrasia. The Eight Days' Fast in honour of the Nativity of Mary begins on Wednesday 1 September.
2027-08-29.verse: For the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life a ransom for many.
theo: In the evening Gospel the mother of James and John kneels before Jesus: “Declare that these two sons of mine will sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your kingdom.” Every mother wants the best for her children. Jesus gently redirects her love: “You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink?” The best a mother can want for her children is not a high seat but a share in Christ's cup of self-giving love.

In Mark's Gospel the brothers ask the same thing themselves. The other ten are angry. Jesus calls them all: “You know that among the Gentiles those whom they recognise as their rulers lord it over them… But it is not so among you; whoever wishes to become great among you must be your servant… For the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life a ransom for many.” The cup Jesus speaks of is his Passion; the ransom is his life given for us.

St Paul sings the same mystery: though he was in the form of God, Christ did not cling to equality with God, but emptied himself, taking the form of a slave; he humbled himself and became obedient to death, even death on a cross; therefore God highly exalted him (Philippians 2:6–9). Mothers know this self-emptying love: nights awake, meals given up, sorrows carried in silence. It is a share in the cup of Christ.

Ezekiel sees water flowing from the side of the temple, getting deeper and deeper, bringing life wherever it goes: “every living creature that swarms will live… on the banks… there will grow all kinds of trees for food… their fruit will be for food, and their leaves for healing.” From the pierced side of Christ, the new temple, flow the waters of Baptism and the Eucharist. From the sacrificial love of mothers flows life into families and the Church.
conn: The Lord their inheritance.
Deuteronomy 18: the Levites have no land; the Lord is their portion. Those who serve find their reward in God.
Faithful service.
2 Chronicles 19:9: “act in the fear of the LORD, in faithfulness, and with your whole heart.”
Water from the temple.
Ezekiel 47 and John 19:34: blood and water from Christ's side.
Serving with gifts.
1 Peter 4:10: like good stewards, serve one another with the gifts you have received.
altar: The cup Jesus offered James and John is the chalice of the altar: his Blood poured out “for many”. To drink it is to commit ourselves to his way of service.
outline: Point 1 · You do not know what you ask
Wanting the best for our children.
Point 2 · Can you drink the cup?
Point 3 · Not to be served but to serve
The love of mothers, a share in Christ's.
“The Son of Man came not to be served but to serve.”
live: Honour your mother
Thank your mother (or pray for her if she has died) in a concrete way this week.
Serve at home
Do a household task usually done by your mother or wife.
Pray during the fast
Pray the Rosary each day until 8 September for all mothers.
fathers: St John Chrysostom

The mother asked out of a mother's affection; Christ did not rebuke her harshly, but turned her request to the cup of suffering, that they might learn that glory comes through the Cross (Homilies on Matthew 65).
St Augustine
He emptied himself, not by losing what he was, but by taking what he was not (Sermon 183).
magis: Catechism 2214–2220
The duty of children toward parents: respect, gratitude, assistance.
Catechism 1551
The ministry of the Church is service, modelled on Christ who came to serve.
Mulieris Dignitatem 18–19 (St John Paul II)
Motherhood involves a special communion with the mystery of life and a special openness to the other person.
saints: 1 September (Wed): the Eight Days' Fast begins. Sunday 5 September: V Sunday after the Transfiguration; St Teresa of Kolkata. 8 September (Wed): Nativity of Mary, Mother of God.
2027-08-29.prayer: Lord Jesus, you came not to be served but to serve and to give your life as a ransom for many. Bless all mothers, who drink your cup of self-giving love; teach us to serve one another; and let the living water from your side bring life wherever we go. Amen.

2027-08-01.title: Eleventh Sunday after Pentecost · Sunday School Day
readings: If your brother listens, you have regained him
The sun of righteousness shall rise
Do not hesitate to visit the sick
God is a God not of disorder but of peace
Jesus sends out the Twelve two by two
2027-08-01.alt: Season of Pentecost. The Fifteen Days' Fast (Shunoyo Nombu) begins today and ends on 15 August, the Assumption of Mary. Mort Shmuni, her seven sons and their teacher Eleazar; St Alphonsus Liguori. Syro-Malankara Catholic Sunday School Day: the Holy Qurbono offering and the cover collection are sent to the eparchial centres for faith formation.
2027-08-01.verse: He will turn the hearts of parents to their children and the hearts of children to their parents.
theo: On the day the Church gives to Sunday school, the readings speak about how faith is passed on: from person to person, from parents to children, from the apostles to the world. In the evening Gospel Jesus teaches the hardest kind of love: “If another member of the church sins against you, go and point out the fault when the two of you are alone. If the member listens to you, you have regained that one.” The aim is not to win an argument but to win back a brother. Leviticus had already joined the two commands together: “you shall reprove your neighbor… but you shall love your neighbor as yourself.”

The same Gospel gives the smallest Church its greatest promise: “where two or three are gathered in my name, I am there among them.” A family that prays together in the evening is such a gathering. A Sunday school class of ten children and one tired teacher is such a gathering. Christ is in the midst of them.

In the Gospel of the Qurbono Jesus sends the Twelve two by two with nothing but a staff. “So they went out and proclaimed that all should repent. They cast out many demons, and anointed with oil many who were sick and cured them.” The Church still anoints the sick with oil in the sacrament of the Anointing. St James adds the test of every faith: “So faith by itself, if it has no works, is dead.” Sirach shows what those works look like: “Do not avoid those who weep, but mourn with those who mourn. Do not hesitate to visit the sick.”

Malachi, the last of the prophets, closes the Old Testament with a promise: “for you who revere my name the sun of righteousness shall rise, with healing in its wings,” and the Lord will send Elijah, who “will turn the hearts of parents to their children and the hearts of children to their parents.” Today we remember a mother whose heart was wholly turned toward her children and toward God: Mort Shmuni, who encouraged her seven sons to die rather than abandon the law of God (2 Maccabees 7). The Fifteen Days' Fast begins today; with Mary, who kept all these things in her heart, let us hand on the faith to the next generation.
conn: Elijah who is to come.

Malachi 4:5–6 is the last word of the prophets. The angel Gabriel quotes it about John the Baptist: he will go “with the spirit and power of Elijah… to turn the hearts of parents to their children” (Luke 1:17).
Reprove and love.
Leviticus 19:17–18 and Matthew 18:15: to correct a brother in private is a form of love, not of hatred.
Anointing with oil.
Mark 6:13 and James 5:14: the apostles anointed the sick; the Church sees here a sign of the sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick.
Mort Shmuni.

The mother of the seven Maccabean martyrs is called Shmuni in the Syriac tradition. Her sons and the old scribe Eleazar (2 Maccabees 6–7) are honoured together on 1 August, the first day of the Fifteen Days' Fast.
altar: “Where two or three are gathered in my name, I am there among them.” At the Holy Qurbono the whole parish, children and teachers, parents and grandparents, gathers in his name, and he is present not only among us but on the altar, given for us. From here we go out, like the Twelve, to heal and to teach.
outline: Sunday School Day: who first taught you to pray?
Point 1 · Go and regain your brother
Correction as an act of love.
Point 2 · Two or three in my name
The family and the class as a little Church.
James and Sirach: visit the sick, weep with those who weep.
Parents and children, teachers and pupils; Mort Shmuni's faith.
“He will turn the hearts of parents to their children.”
live: Thank a teacher
Thank (or pray for) the catechist who first taught you the faith (Malachi 4:6).
Pray as a family
Gather as a family each evening of the fast for a short prayer (Matthew 18:20).
One work of mercy
Visit one sick or grieving person during the Fifteen Days' Fast (Sirach 7:34–35).
fathers: St Augustine
If your brother has sinned against you and you alone know it, correct him between you and him alone: seek to gain him, not to shame him (Sermon 82).
St John Chrysostom
Preaching on the mother of the Maccabees, he praised her as a mother who gave birth to her sons twice: once to this life, and again, by her encouragement, to eternal life (Homilies on the Maccabees).
magis: Catechism 2221–2226
Parents are the first educators of their children in the faith; the family is a domestic church.
Catechism 1815 and 1829
“Faith apart from works is dead”; charity demands beneficence and fraternal correction.
Catechesi Tradendae 68 (St John Paul II)
Family catechesis precedes, accompanies and enriches all other forms of catechesis.
saints: 1 August: Mort Shmuni, her seven sons and Eleazar; St Alphonsus Liguori; the Fifteen Days' Fast begins. 4 August: St John Mary Vianney. 5 August: anniversary of the Eparchy of Parassala (2017). 6 August (Fri): the Transfiguration of Our Lord.
2027-08-01.prayer: Lord Jesus, you promised to be among us when we gather in your name. Bless our Sunday school teachers and children, our parents and grandparents. Turn the hearts of parents to their children and the hearts of children to their parents. Give us courage to correct in love, a faith that works, and hearts that visit the sick and weep with those who weep. Through the prayers of Mary, whose Assumption we await in this fast, and of Mort Shmuni and her sons. Amen.

quick: Jesus is transfigured while praying; the Law and the Prophets speak of his Cross.
“This is my Son, my Chosen; listen to him!”
The light of Tabor is the glory Christ will share with us.
2027-08-06.action: Spend fifteen minutes in silent prayer today.
2027-08-06.question: Do I really listen to Jesus?
2027-08-06.special: Transfiguration of Our Lord (Friday). The season of the Transfiguration begins.
illus: Pilgrims climb Mount Tabor in Galilee to the Basilica of the Transfiguration. At the top the view opens over the whole valley. Prayer does that: it lifts us up to see our lives as God sees them.

family.explain: On a mountain Jesus' face shone like the sun, and God the Father said: “This is my Son. Listen to him!”
family.intention: We pray to listen to Jesus every day.
family.ask: Ask: “What is Jesus asking our family to do?”

kidsaint: A deacon in Rome who took care of the poor. When the emperor demanded the Church's treasures, Lawrence brought the poor and said: “These are the treasures of the Church.” He was martyred in 258. Lesson: the poor are the Church's treasure.
term: The name used in the Syro-Malankara lectionary for the feast of the Transfiguration (6 August). The Syriac word is generally linked with “tents” or “booths”, recalling Peter's three tents and the Feast of Booths.
termMore: The sixth season of the Syro-Malankara year, from 6 August to the feast of the Holy Cross (14 September): a time to contemplate Christ's glory and prepare for his final coming.

quick: The two sons: obedience counts more than words.
A lamp is put on the lampstand: faith is not to be hidden.
“Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you.”
2027-08-08.action: Do one thing this week that you have been refusing God.
2027-08-08.question: Am I the son who says yes and does not go?
2027-08-08.special: First Sunday after the Transfiguration. Remind the faithful of the Shunoyo next Sunday, 15 August.
illus: In a Kerala market a fish seller was known for one thing: her scale was always honest. People walked past cheaper stalls to buy from her. Without a sermon, her weights preached the Gospel.

family.explain: One son said “No” but then went to help his father. The other said “Yes” but didn't go. Jesus wants us to say yes and do it!
family.intention: We pray to obey God not only with words but with actions.
family.ask: Ask: “What did we promise to do this week? Have we done it?”

kidsaint: A Polish priest who loved Mary very much. In the concentration camp of Auschwitz he offered to die in place of a father of a family. He was martyred in 1941. Lesson: true love says “yes” with actions.
term: The Sundays after 6 August, during which the Syro-Malankara lectionary reads parables of the kingdom and calls to faithful living, in the light of Christ's glory and his coming.
termMore: Syriac for “departure”: the feast of the Dormition and Assumption of the Mother of God (15 August), preceded by a fifteen-day fast.

quick: Mary, having completed her earthly life, was assumed body and soul into heaven.
She is the living Ark who carried the Word; today the Ark enters the promised land.
“Here is your mother”: take Mary into your home.
2027-08-15.action: Pray the Rosary together as a family tonight.
2027-08-15.question: Have I taken Mary into my home, as the beloved disciple did?
2027-08-15.special: Shunoyo, the Assumption of Mary (Sunday): Holy Qurbono for the people; end of the Fifteen Days' Fast. Independence Day of India. Founding of Bethany Ashram (1919).
illus: In many Kerala homes on 15 August the family breaks the fast together after Holy Qurbono, and the flag of India flies over the house. Mary's freedom from corruption and our country's freedom meet on one day; both are gifts to be lived well.

family.explain: From the Cross Jesus gave his mother to his disciple, and to us. Today we celebrate that Mary went to heaven, body and soul, to be with Jesus.
family.intention: We pray to Mary to take care of our family and our country.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we make Mary part of our home?”

kidsaint: Mary said “yes” to God and became the mother of Jesus. She stayed near him even at the Cross. At the end of her life, God took her body and soul to heaven. Lesson: Mary is our mother in heaven who prays for us.
term: The dogma defined by Pope Pius XII on 1 November 1950: Mary, at the end of her earthly life, was taken up body and soul into heavenly glory. The East celebrates the same mystery as the Dormition (Shunoyo).
termMore: The gold-covered chest in the tabernacle and Temple holding the tablets of the Law, a jar of manna and Aaron's rod (Hebrews 9:4). The Church calls Mary the “Ark of the Covenant” in her litany because she carried the Lord himself.

quick: The tax collector, not the proud Pharisee, went home justified.
“God, be merciful to me, a sinner”: the Jesus Prayer.
“My grace is sufficient for you; power is made perfect in weakness.”
2027-08-22.action: Pray the Jesus Prayer many times each day this week.
2027-08-22.question: Do I pray like the Pharisee or like the tax collector?
2027-08-22.special: Third Sunday after the Transfiguration. Announce the Eight Days' Fast (1–8 September) before the Nativity of Mary.
illus: An old man in a Kerala parish always sat at the back of the church, head bowed, beating his breast at the Kurielaison. People thought he was a great sinner. After his death they learned he had quietly paid the school fees of dozens of poor children. Humility hides its goodness and confesses its sin.

family.explain: One man prayed proudly: “I'm better than others.” Another prayed humbly: “God, have mercy on me.” God was pleased with the humble prayer.
family.intention: We pray for humble hearts that ask God's mercy.
family.ask: Ask: “Why does God love a humble prayer?”

kidsaint: John told the truth even to King Herod, who had done wrong. He was put in prison and beheaded. John always said: “He must increase, but I must decrease.” Lesson: be humble and brave for the truth.
term: Greek for “Lord, have mercy”, sung many times in the Syro-Malankara Qurbono and prayers. It echoes the tax collector's prayer and the cries of the blind and sick in the Gospels.
termMore: A popular fast kept from 1 to 8 September in Kerala in preparation for the feast of the Nativity of Mary (8 September), with prayer, Rosary and pilgrimage to Marian shrines.

quick: The mother of James and John asked for high seats; Jesus offered his cup.
“The Son of Man came not to be served but to serve.”
Christ emptied himself; mothers share in his self-giving love.
2027-08-29.action: Thank your mother in a concrete way this week, or pray for her soul.
2027-08-29.question: Do I seek to be served, or to serve?
2027-08-29.special: Fourth Sunday after the Transfiguration. (In 2025–26: Malankara Catholic Mothers' Forum Day. Check your eparchy's circular.) Eight Days' Fast continues.
illus: A Kerala mother in the Gulf works as a nurse on night shifts so that her children at home can study. She sees them for one month a year. When her son was ordained a priest, she said: “His chalice is my cup too.”

family.explain: Jesus said that the greatest person is the one who serves others, just as he served us and gave his life for us.
family.intention: We pray for our mothers and grandmothers.
family.ask: Ask: “How can each of us serve the family this week?”

kidsaint: A sister from Albania who came to India and served the poorest of the poor in the streets of Kolkata, caring for the dying and abandoned babies. She was called “Mother” by everyone. Lesson: being great means serving others with love.
term: The Malankara Catholic Mothers' Forum, an association of mothers in the Syro-Malankara Church for prayer, faith formation, family life and charity.
termMore: In the Bible “the cup” can mean one's destiny from God. Jesus speaks of the cup of his Passion (Mark 10:38; 14:36), which becomes the chalice of the New Covenant in his Blood.

quick: Sunday School Day: faith is handed on person to person.
“Where two or three are gathered in my name, I am there among them.”
“Faith by itself, if it has no works, is dead.”
2027-08-01.action: Thank or pray for the catechist who first taught you the faith.
2027-08-01.question: Who did I learn the faith from, and to whom am I handing it on?
2027-08-01.special: Eleventh Sunday after Pentecost. Sunday School Day: the offering and cover collection go to the eparchial centre for faith formation. The Fifteen Days' Fast (Shunoyo Nombu) begins today.
illus: A grandmother in Kerala could not read well, but every evening she sat on the veranda with her grandchildren and the rosary. Years later one of them, now an engineer in Germany, said at her funeral: “I learned the faith in Sunday school, but I learned to love God on her veranda.”

family.explain: Jesus promised that when two or three people pray together in his name, he is right there with them. When our family prays, Jesus is in the middle of us.
family.intention: We pray for our Sunday school teachers and for all the children of our parish.
family.ask: Ask: “What time can we pray together every evening during the fast?”

catechism: Parents as first educators in faith.
The Anointing of the Sick, alluded to in Mark 6:13.
kidsaint: Mort Shmuni and her seven sons (1 August)

In the time of the Maccabees a cruel king tried to force the Jews to break God's law. A mother and her seven sons refused. One by one the sons were killed, and the mother encouraged each of them to stay faithful to God, because God would raise them up. The Syriac tradition calls her Shmuni. Lesson: a brave mother can teach her children to love God more than anything.
term: The Fifteen Days' Fast, from 1 to 15 August, in preparation for the feast of the Assumption (Shunoyo, the “passing” of Mary). The faithful fast, pray and give alms with Mary.
termMore: The parish school of faith formation for children, held on Sundays around the Holy Qurbono. On Sunday School Day the offering supports catechesis in the eparchy.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, Jesus took Peter, John and James up a mountain to pray. And while he was praying, his face changed and his clothes became dazzling white. For a moment the disciples saw who he really is: the Son of God, full of glory.

Moses and Elijah appeared and spoke with him. About what? About “his departure, which he was about to accomplish at Jerusalem”, that is, his Passion and death. On the mountain of glory they speak of the Cross. The Transfiguration was given to strengthen the disciples, so that when they saw Jesus disfigured on Calvary they would remember Tabor.

Peter wanted to stay: “It is good for us to be here; let us make three tents.” But a cloud covered them, and the Father spoke: “This is my Son, my Chosen; listen to him!” Then they saw only Jesus. The Christian life is not about staying on the mountain; it is about listening to Jesus and going down with him to serve.

The light of Tabor is also our future. St Paul says we shall be changed into his likeness. Every Holy Qurbono is a little Tabor: we go up to the altar, we see the Lord with the eyes of faith, and we come down to live his word. Today, climb the mountain: spend fifteen minutes in silence with the Lord, and listen to him. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus went up a mountain with three friends. While he prayed, his face shone like the sun and his clothes became bright white!
Then a cloud came and God the Father said: “This is my Son. Listen to him!”
How can we listen to Jesus? By reading the Bible and doing what he says. Let's be good listeners!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a father had two sons. He asked the first to work in his vineyard; the son said “No,” but later changed his mind and went. He asked the second; the son said “Yes, sir,” but did not go. Jesus asks: which one did the father's will? We all know the answer. And we all know which son we often resemble.

How often we say “yes” to God: at our Baptism, in our marriage vows, at our ordination or profession, every time we say “Amen” in the Qurbono. And how often that yes stays on our lips. Jesus is not impressed by words. But there is great hope here too: the son who first said “no” could still change his mind. It is never too late to go into the vineyard.

In the evening Gospel Jesus says a lamp is put on a lampstand, not under a basket. Our faith must be seen, not in show, but in honest living. Deuteronomy says: “You shall have only a full and honest weight.” In our shops, offices and farms, honest measures preach the Gospel better than words.

St James says: draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Next Sunday we celebrate the Shunoyo of our Mother, who said “Let it be to me according to your word” and lived it to the end. This week, take one “no” you have been saying to God and turn it into “yes”. Amen.
kids: Children, a father asked two sons to help him. The first said “No!” but then he went and helped. The second said “Yes!” but didn't go.
Which son made the father happy? Yes, the one who actually helped!
When mum or dad asks you to help, don't just say “yes”, do it! That's how we obey God too.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today is the Shunoyo, the day our Mother departed this life and was taken into heaven. Our Eastern tradition sings of her “falling asleep”; the Catholic Church teaches with certainty that Mary, having finished the course of her earthly life, was taken up body and soul into the glory of heaven. The womb that carried God was not left to decay.

The readings speak of the ark. When the priests carried the ark into the Jordan, the waters parted and the people crossed into the promised land. The ark carried the tablets of the Law and the manna. Mary carried the Word of God and the true Bread from heaven. She is the living Ark, and today the Ark crosses the river of death into the promised land of heaven.

At the Cross Jesus gave her to us: “Here is your mother.” And the disciple took her into his home. Have we taken her into ours? Is there a place for her in our family prayer, our decisions, our sorrows? And Jesus also said: whoever does the will of my Father is my mother and sister and brother. Mary is great because she did God's will perfectly.

Today is also Independence Day, eighty years of a free India. Let us pray to our Mother for our nation: for justice, for peace, for the poor, for freedom of faith. And let us live as people whose bodies too are destined for glory: with purity, with dignity, with love. Holy Mother of God, pray for us. Amen.
kids: Children, today we celebrate that Mother Mary went to heaven, body and soul, to be with Jesus!
Jesus gave Mary to us as our mother when he was on the Cross. She loves us and prays for us.
Let's pray the Hail Mary together today, and thank God for our country India too!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, two men went up to the temple to pray. The Pharisee stood and listed his good works: I fast twice a week, I give tithes, and I thank you that I am not like other people, especially this tax collector. The tax collector stood far off, did not dare raise his eyes, beat his breast and prayed: “God, be merciful to me, a sinner!” Jesus says: the second went home justified.

The Pharisee was not a bad man. He did many good things. But his prayer was about himself, and it ended in contempt for his neighbour. The tax collector had nothing to boast about, and so he had room for God's mercy. St Augustine says: the Pharisee showed the doctor only his healthy parts; the tax collector showed his wounds, and so he was healed.

The tax collector's prayer became the Jesus Prayer of our Eastern tradition: “Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner.” It is short, as Ecclesiastes advises: “let your words be few.” And in the evening Gospel Jesus teaches us to be persistent: ask, search, knock, like the friend at midnight. Humble prayer is not timid; it keeps knocking.

St Paul learned the same lesson. He asked God three times to take away his thorn, and God answered: “My grace is sufficient for you; my power is made perfect in weakness.” This week, pray the Jesus Prayer often, stop comparing yourself with others, and prepare for the Eight Days' Fast in honour of our Mother. Amen.
kids: Children, two men went to pray. One said: “God, I'm so good, better than him!” The other said: “God, I'm sorry, please be kind to me.”
Jesus said God was happy with the second man, because he was humble.
Let's learn a short prayer: “Jesus, Son of God, have mercy on me.” You can say it anytime!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a mother came to Jesus and knelt before him with her two sons. She asked: let my sons sit at your right and your left in your kingdom. What mother does not want the best for her children? Jesus did not scold her. He said: “You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink?”

The other disciples were angry. So Jesus called them together and said: the rulers of the nations lord it over people; it shall not be so among you. Whoever wants to be great must be your servant. “For the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life a ransom for many.” That is the cup: the self-giving love that goes all the way to the Cross.

St Paul says Christ emptied himself and took the form of a servant. Who understands this better than mothers? Sleepless nights, meals given up, tears hidden, prayers said for children far away. Our mothers drink the cup of Christ every day. Today we honour them, and we thank God for them.

Ezekiel saw water flowing from the temple, bringing life wherever it went. From the side of Christ on the Cross flowed blood and water, the life of the Church. From the love of mothers flows life into our families. This week, honour your mother, serve at home, and let us pray during the Eight Days' Fast for all mothers, through Mary, the Mother of God. Amen.
kids: Children, a mother asked Jesus to give her sons the best seats in heaven. Jesus said the best thing is to serve others with love.
Jesus said: “I came not to be served but to serve.” He even gave his life for us!
Your mother serves you every day. How can you serve her this week? Give her a big thank you!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today is Sunday School Day. Who first taught you to make the sign of the cross? A mother, a grandmother, a Sunday school teacher in a small classroom? Faith is not downloaded; it is handed on, person to person, heart to heart. The last prophet, Malachi, promised that God would “turn the hearts of parents to their children and the hearts of children to their parents.” That is what every good home and every good Sunday school does.

In the Gospel Jesus teaches us to correct one another with love: go to your brother alone, point out the fault, and if he listens, “you have regained that one.” Not to shame him, but to win him back. Teachers do this every week with patience. Parents do it every day. And Jesus adds a promise: “where two or three are gathered in my name, I am there among them.” A family praying at night is a little Church.

Jesus sent the Twelve two by two. They preached repentance, cast out demons and anointed the sick with oil. St James says faith without works is dead. Sirach says: do not avoid those who weep; do not hesitate to visit the sick. Our children learn the faith not only from what we say but from what they see us do.

Today the Fifteen Days' Fast begins, and we remember Mort Shmuni, the mother of seven sons who chose God above everything. Let us thank our catechists, support the Sunday school generously, and pray together as families every evening of this fast, with Mary, the Mother of God. Amen.
kids: Children, today is your day: Sunday School Day! Thank your teachers, who give their Sundays to teach you about Jesus.
Jesus said: when two or three pray together in my name, I am with them. When you pray with your family at night, Jesus is right there.
Today a fast of fifteen days begins, before Mary's feast. Can you say one Hail Mary every day for your teacher?

intro: Theme: “This is my Son, my Chosen; listen to him!”
On the mountain the glory of the Son shines through his humanity. Moses and Elijah speak with him about his departure in Jerusalem. The glory is revealed to strengthen the disciples for the Cross.

sub: Moses' face shone after speaking with God; Jesus' face shines with his own divine glory.
The Transfiguration reveals who Jesus is: true God and true man.
It also shows what we are called to become: transformed by grace.
q: Moses came down from Mount Sinai. As he came down from the mountain with the two tablets of the covenant in his hand, Moses did not know that the skin of his face shone because he had been talking with God.
And he was transfigured before them, and his face shone like the sun, and his clothes became dazzling white.
points.apply: Spend time in prayer before the Lord this week, and let him change you.

sub: Moses promised a prophet like himself, whom the people must heed.
The Father's voice confirms: Jesus is that Prophet and more, the beloved Son.
Moses and Elijah, the Law and the Prophets, point to him.
q: The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you shall heed such a prophet.
Then from the cloud came a voice that said, “This is my Son, my Chosen; listen to him!”
points.apply: Before each decision this week ask: what does Jesus say about this?

sub: On the mountain they speak of his “departure”: his Passion in Jerusalem.
The disciples see the glory so that they will not lose faith when they see the Cross.
Isaiah's promise is fulfilled: the Lord himself is our everlasting light.
q: The sun shall no longer be your light by day, nor for brightness shall the moon give light to you by night; but the LORD will be your everlasting light, and your God will be your glory.
And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory as of a father's only son, full of grace and truth.
points.apply: Offer one present suffering to the Lord, trusting that it leads to glory.

concl: The Transfiguration gives us a glimpse of Easter in the middle of the journey to the Cross.
Let us listen to the Son and let his light transform us.
2027-08-06.resolve: Keep the rest of the Fifteen Days' Fast faithfully, with Mary.

intro: Theme: “Not words, but the Father's will.”
Two sons: one refuses but later goes; the other promises but does not go. Elijah on Carmel challenges the people to stop limping between two opinions. God asks for an undivided and honest heart.

sub: The son who first refused later changed his mind and went: conversion is always possible.
The son who said “I go, sir” and did not go is the danger of empty religion.
Tax collectors and prostitutes who repent enter the kingdom ahead of the self-satisfied.
q: Again, when the wicked turn away from the wickedness they have committed and do what is lawful and right, they shall save their life.
“Which of the two did the will of his father?” They said, “The first.” Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, the tax collectors and the prostitutes are going into the kingdom of God ahead of you.”
points.apply: Keep one promise to God that you have postponed.

points.h: No more limping between two opinions
sub: Elijah: “If the LORD is God, follow him.”
Fire falls from heaven and the people cry: “The LORD indeed is God!”
James: draw near to God and he will draw near to you; purify your hearts, you double-minded.
q: Elijah then came near to all the people, and said, “How long will you go limping with two different opinions? If the LORD is God, follow him; but if Baal, then follow him.” The people did not answer him a word.
Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded.
points.apply: Identify one “Baal” that competes with God in your life and renounce it.

sub: God's law required honest weights and measures.
Holiness reaches our business, our accounts and our words.
Paul: think about whatever is true, honourable, just and pure.
q: You shall have only a full and honest weight; you shall have only a full and honest measure, so that your days may be long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.

Finally, beloved, whatever is true, whatever is honorable, whatever is just, whatever is pure, whatever is pleasing, whatever is commendable, if there is any excellence and if there is anything worthy of praise, think about these things.
points.apply: Correct one dishonest practice in your work or home, however small.

concl: God looks for sons and daughters who do his will with an undivided, honest heart.
Let our yes to God be a real yes.
2027-08-08.resolve: Examine your conscience each night this week on honesty in word and deed.

intro: Theme: “The Mother taken up to glory.”

Today we celebrate the Shunoyo, the passing of the Mother of God. The Church teaches as revealed dogma that the Immaculate Mother of God, the ever-Virgin Mary, having completed the course of her earthly life, was assumed body and soul into heavenly glory (Pius XII, Munificentissimus Deus, 1950). The Fifteen Days' Fast ends; it is also India's Independence Day.

sub: After the Fall God promised enmity between the serpent and the woman.
Mary, the New Eve, is the woman whose Son crushes the serpent.
In Revelation the woman clothed with the sun shows her glory with her Son.
q: I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; he will strike your head, and you will strike his heel.
A great portent appeared in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars.
points.apply: Pray the Hail Mary slowly today, thinking of her victory with Christ.

points.h: The Queen at the King's right hand
sub: The psalm sings of the queen standing at the king's right hand.
Mary, the lowly handmaid, is exalted; God has done great things for her.
Her Assumption is the first fruit of Christ's Resurrection and the sign of our hope (CCC 966).
q: Daughters of kings are among your ladies of honor; at your right hand stands the queen in gold of Ophir.
For he has looked with favor on the lowliness of his servant. Surely, from now on all generations will call me blessed; for the Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy is his name.
points.apply: Look at your own body with reverence: it is destined for resurrection.

sub: From the Cross Jesus gave his Mother to the beloved disciple, and to all of us.
She who did the will of the Father is mother of all who do it.
From heaven she continues to intercede for us.
q: I will greatly rejoice in the LORD, my whole being shall exult in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, he has covered me with the robe of righteousness.

When Jesus saw his mother and the disciple whom he loved standing beside her, he said to his mother, “Woman, here is your son.” Then he said to the disciple, “Here is your mother.” And from that hour the disciple took her into his own home.
points.apply: Take Mary “into your home”: renew family consecration to her today.

concl: Where Mary has gone, the Church hopes to follow.
Let us thank God for our Mother in glory, and pray for our nation on Independence Day.
2027-08-15.resolve: Pray the Rosary as a family for India and for peace this week.

intro: Theme: “God, be merciful to me, a sinner!”

Two men pray in the temple: one boasts, the other begs for mercy. Jesus teaches us to ask, seek and knock. Today is also the memorial of the Beheading of St John the Baptist, who said: “He must increase, but I must decrease.”

sub: The Pharisee prays about himself and despises others.
The tax collector stands far off, beats his breast and asks for mercy.
God does not despise a broken and contrite heart; this prayer is at the heart of our liturgy: “Lord, have mercy.”
q: The sacrifice acceptable to God is a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise.

But the tax collector, standing far off, would not even look up to heaven, but was beating his breast and saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner!’ I tell you, this man went down to his home justified rather than the other.
points.apply: Pray the tax collector's prayer several times each day this week.

sub: Jesus urges persistence in prayer, like the friend at midnight.
The Father gives good gifts, above all the Holy Spirit.
Through waters and fire God is with those who call on him.
q: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and through the rivers, they shall not overwhelm you; when you walk through fire you shall not be burned, and the flame shall not consume you.
So I say to you, Ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you.
points.apply: Ask the Father daily this week for a fresh outpouring of the Holy Spirit.

sub: Noah found favour with God, not through his own power but through God's grace.
Paul learned: “My grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness.”
John the Baptist decreased so that Christ might increase, even to martyrdom.
q: But Noah found favor in the sight of the LORD.
But he said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness.” So, I will boast all the more gladly of my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may dwell in me.
points.apply: Offer one weakness to God, and let his grace work through it.

concl: The humble are lifted up, the persistent are heard, the weak are made strong by grace.
Let us pray as the tax collector, trust like Noah, and decrease like John.
2027-08-22.resolve: Prepare for the Eight Days' Fast (1–8 September) in honour of Mary's Nativity.

intro: Theme: “Not to be served but to serve.”

A mother asks Jesus for the places of honour for her two sons. Jesus answers with the cup of suffering and the way of service. In the 2025–26 lectionary this was Mothers' Forum Day; the Eight Days' Fast in honour of Mary continues.

sub: Among the nations rulers lord it over others; “it is not so among you.”
Whoever wishes to be great must be servant; whoever wishes to be first must be slave of all.
Jesus gives the reason: he himself came to serve and give his life.
q: He charged them: “This is how you shall act: in the fear of the LORD, in faithfulness, and with your whole heart.”

But whoever wishes to become great among you must be your servant, and whoever wishes to be first among you must be slave of all. For the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life a ransom for many.
points.apply: Do one humble service at home this week that usually falls to someone else.

sub: The mother of James and John loves her sons and wants the best for them.
Jesus does not reject her love but purifies it: true honour is to share his cup.
Christian mothers pray not only for their children's success but for their holiness.
q: Charm is deceitful, and beauty is vain, but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.

And he said to her, “What do you want?” She said to him, “Declare that these two sons of mine will sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your kingdom.” But Jesus answered, “You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink?” They said to him, “We are able.”
points.apply: Mothers: pray each day this week for the holiness of each of your children by name.

sub: Christ, though in the form of God, emptied himself and took the form of a slave.
Like the river from the temple in Ezekiel, his self-giving brings life wherever it flows.
Each of us must serve others with the gift we have received.
q: Wherever the river goes, every living creature that swarms will live, and there will be very many fish, once these waters reach there. It will become fresh; and everything will live where the river goes.
Who, though he was in the form of God, did not regard equality with God as something to be exploited, but emptied himself, taking the form of a slave, being born in human likeness.
points.apply: Offer your particular gift (time, skill, money) to a parish ministry.

concl: In the kingdom the first are servants and the greatest are those who give their lives.
Let us follow the Servant Lord with Mary, the handmaid of the Lord.
2027-08-29.resolve: Keep the remaining days of the Eight Days' Fast with a daily act of service.

intro: Theme: “He will turn the hearts of parents to their children.”
Sunday School Day: faith is handed on person to person, through loving correction, prayer together and works of mercy. The Fifteen Days' Fast begins.

sub: Correction is an act of love, not of victory.
Go alone first; the aim is to win back a brother.
Leviticus joins reproof and love together.
q: You shall not hate in your heart anyone of your kin; you shall reprove your neighbor, or you will incur guilt yourself. You shall not take vengeance or bear a grudge against any of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself: I am the LORD.
If another member of the church sins against you, go and point out the fault when the two of you are alone. If the member listens to you, you have regained that one.
points.apply: Is there someone you need to speak to gently and privately? Pray, then go.

points.h: Two or three in my name
sub: The smallest gathering in Christ's name has his presence.
A family praying at night is a little Church.
A Sunday school class is such a gathering too.
q: Keep these words that I am commanding you today in your heart. Recite them to your children and talk about them when you are at home and when you are away, when you lie down and when you rise.
For where two or three are gathered in my name, I am there among them.
points.apply: Gather as a family each evening of the fast for a short prayer.

sub: Faith without works is dead.
Sirach shows the works: weep with those who weep, visit the sick.
The Twelve anointed the sick; the Church still does in the sacrament of Anointing.
q: Do not avoid those who weep, but mourn with those who mourn. Do not hesitate to visit the sick, because for such deeds you will be loved.
So faith by itself, if it has no works, is dead.
points.apply: Visit one sick or grieving person during the Fifteen Days' Fast.

sub: Malachi's promise closes the Old Testament.
Parents and children, teachers and pupils: hearts turned to one another and to God.
Mort Shmuni encouraged her seven sons to stay faithful to God (2 Maccabees 7).
q: He will turn the hearts of parents to their children and the hearts of children to their parents.
So they went out and proclaimed that all should repent. They cast out many demons, and anointed with oil many who were sick and cured them.
points.apply: Thank, or pray for, the catechist who first taught you the faith.

concl: Faith is not downloaded; it is handed on, heart to heart.
With Mary, who kept all these things in her heart, let us hand on the faith to the next generation.
2027-08-01.resolve: Keep the Fifteen Days' Fast with daily family prayer and one work of mercy.
